def boot(self) -> int:
        """Boot the kernel. Creates root task. Returns root task ID."""
        with self._lock:
            self._running = True
            root = self._create_task_internal("root", parent_id=-1, priority=0)
            # Root gets a wildcard capability
            self._grant_cap(root, "task", 0, {"create", "destroy"})
            log.info("Daisy Kernel %s (%s) booted. Root task: %d",
                     self.VERSION, self.CODENAME, root)
            return root
issues.problem: boot() is not idempotent. Every call creates another root task and mutates kernel state while the existing task table remains live.
issues.failure_scenario: A service that retries boot after a partial startup creates multiple root tasks with root capabilities, making scheduling and capability ownership inconsistent.
issues.fix_instruction: Guard boot() with the kernel lock. If the kernel is already running, either return the existing root task ID or raise KernelError; do not create another root task.

        self._root_task_id = root_tid

        """Download an update image to cache."""

        dest = os.path.join(UPDATE_CACHE, filename)

        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "curl", "-fSL", "-o", dest, url,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,

/// Physical address where the kernel is expected to be loaded.

issues.problem: The bootloader defines a fixed kernel load address but never loads kernel.elf into that address before jumping to it.
issues.failure_scenario: UEFI exits boot services and jumps to unmapped or uninitialized memory at 0x100000, causing immediate boot failure.
issues.fix_instruction: Before exit_boot_services, open the kernel ELF from the ESP, parse PT_LOAD segments, allocate pages, copy segments to memory, zero BSS, and jump to the ELF entry point.

issues.problem: BootInfo passed by the bootloader lacks the memory map address, descriptor size, and map key details the kernel needs after ExitBootServices.
issues.failure_scenario: The kernel cannot safely initialize physical memory management from the UEFI map.
issues.fix_instruction: Extend BootInfo with memory map pointer, byte length, descriptor size, and framebuffer details; keep the struct definition shared with the kernel.

issues.problem: The QEMU script swallows bootloader build failures and continues.
issues.failure_scenario: QEMU can start with no BOOTX64.EFI, producing a confusing non-bootable VM instead of a clear build failure.
issues.fix_instruction: Fail fast if the bootloader build fails or the EFI binary is missing.

issues.problem: Kernel BootInfo has no #[repr(C)] even though the UEFI bootloader passes a C-layout struct pointer across the boot boundary.
issues.failure_scenario: Rust may lay out the kernel struct differently than the bootloader struct, so framebuffer and memory fields can be read incorrectly.
issues.fix_instruction: Add #[repr(C)] and keep this struct in exact field order with the bootloader, preferably through a shared crate.

issues.problem: timer_preempt() creates a new empty Scheduler every tick, so it never selects runnable tasks from the real run queue.
issues.failure_scenario: Timer interrupts do not preempt running tasks; multitasking appears initialized but no context switch occurs.
issues.fix_instruction: Wire timer_preempt() to the global scheduler/task state and select the next runnable task from the real queue.

issues.problem: Task contexts and stacks are global mutable statics without synchronization or interrupt discipline.
issues.failure_scenario: An interrupt or second CPU can mutate task context state while a switch or spawn operation is in progress, corrupting register state.
issues.fix_instruction: Protect task tables with an interrupt-safe lock or enforce single-core/non-preemptible access around all mutations.
issues.suggested_code:
// Replace static mut arrays with an UnsafeCell-backed table guarded by
// an interrupt-safe spin::Mutex, and never expose shared references to it.

issues.code_snippet:
/// PRNG seed for /dev/random.
static SEED: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(12345);
issues.problem: /dev/random uses a fixed-seed linear congruential generator.
issues.failure_scenario: Any consumer using /dev/random for secrets receives predictable bytes.
issues.fix_instruction: Do not expose deterministic bytes as random. Seed a CSPRNG from hardware/bootloader entropy or rename this device to a clearly non-cryptographic test RNG.
issues.suggested_code:
// Until real entropy exists, make reads from /dev/random return EAGAIN or
// expose this only as /dev/pseudorandom-test with clear non-crypto semantics.

issues.problem: E1000 init logs success and sets initialized=true without descriptor rings or working TX/RX.
issues.failure_scenario: The network stack believes a NIC is ready, but send/receive calls fail or drop packets.
issues.fix_instruction: Only set initialized after TX/RX descriptor rings, buffers, interrupts, and MAC configuration are complete.
issues.suggested_code:
// Set initialized only after descriptor setup succeeds:
// setup_tx_ring()?; setup_rx_ring()?; enable_rx_tx(); NIC.initialized = true;

issues.problem: ELF segment loading writes directly to p_vaddr from the ELF program header without validating that the virtual range is allowed, mapped, non-overlapping, or that memsz >= filesz.
issues.failure_scenario: A malformed or malicious ELF can make the loader overwrite arbitrary kernel memory or copy more initialized bytes than the memory segment declares.
issues.fix_instruction: Validate every PT_LOAD segment before copying: memsz >= filesz, address range is user/loadable, pages are allocated/mapped, alignment is valid, and segments do not overlap.

issues.problem: cluster_to_lba() panics on invalid cluster numbers with assert! instead of returning an error.
issues.failure_scenario: A malformed FAT chain can panic the kernel while reading a filesystem.
issues.fix_instruction: Return Result<u64, FatError> from cluster_to_lba and propagate invalid-cluster errors to callers.

issues.problem: Directory reading only supports clusters up to 4096 bytes, but valid FAT32 volumes commonly use larger clusters.
issues.failure_scenario: Valid FAT32 filesystems with 8 KiB or larger clusters fail with UnsupportedClusterSize.
issues.fix_instruction: Read directory clusters sector-by-sector or allocate a buffer sized to cluster_size from the heap.

issues.problem: The global allocator never frees memory.
issues.failure_scenario: Any subsystem using alloc after boot leaks permanently; repeated allocations can exhaust the kernel heap.
issues.fix_instruction: Use the bump allocator only for early boot, then switch to a real free-list/slab allocator before long-lived services allocate.

issues.problem: Boot initializes multiple drivers that are stubbed or explicitly nonfunctional, but the boot log does not distinguish unavailable features.
issues.failure_scenario: The system appears to have storage/network/USB support even though NVMe, E1000, and parts of the stack cannot perform I/O.
issues.fix_instruction: Return and log explicit feature status for each driver, and keep unimplemented drivers disabled until the backing operations work.
issues.suggested_code:
let nvme_available = nvme::init();
if !nvme_available { vga::print_warning('NVMe disabled: driver incomplete'); }

issues.problem: kernel_main() ends in a keyboard echo/hlt loop with no scheduler start, init process launch, or syscall/user mode transition.
issues.failure_scenario: The OS boots but never starts userspace or scheduled kernel tasks.
issues.fix_instruction: After hardware init, initialize syscall entry, mount the root filesystem, create/init the first task, and enter the scheduler idle loop.

issues.problem: ARP and ICMP receive handlers only log TODO messages and never send replies.
issues.failure_scenario: Other hosts cannot resolve Daisy over ARP or receive ping responses, so network connectivity appears dead.
issues.fix_instruction: Do not advertise the network stack as functional until ARP reply and ICMP echo response transmission are implemented via the NIC driver.
issues.suggested_code:
// Implement ARP reply and ICMP echo reply once e1000::send_packet works;
// otherwise report networking as receive-only/unimplemented.

issues.problem: NVMe initialization explicitly does not allocate queues and then sets initialized=false before returning false.
issues.failure_scenario: Any boot path expecting NVMe storage will always fail even when an NVMe controller exists.
issues.fix_instruction: Either feature-gate NVMe as unimplemented or implement admin and I/O queue allocation before reporting initialization status.
issues.suggested_code:
// Do not advertise NVMe until queues are live:
// allocate_admin_queues(...)?; identify_controller(...)?; identify_namespace(...)?; NVME.initialized = true;

issues.code_snippet:
"mov rdi, rax",    // arg0 = syscall number
            "mov rsi, rdi",    // arg1 = original rdi (first user arg)
            "call {dispatch}",
issues.problem: The syscall entry assembly overwrites the original first argument in rdi with the syscall number, then copies that syscall number into rsi.
issues.failure_scenario: Every syscall dispatch receives the wrong first user argument and cannot correctly implement Linux-style syscall calling conventions.
issues.fix_instruction: Save user argument registers before clobbering them and pass syscall number plus all arguments to one syscall dispatcher.
issues.suggested_code:
// Preserve user rdi before overwriting it. Dispatch as:
// dispatch(sysno=rax, arg0=rdi, arg1=rsi, arg2=rdx, arg3=r10, arg4=r8, arg5=r9)

issues.problem: syscall.rs defines a syscall dispatch table that conflicts with syscall_table.rs numbering and behavior.
issues.failure_scenario: Userland can receive different behavior depending on which syscall path is wired, making ABI compatibility impossible.
issues.fix_instruction: Delete one dispatcher or make syscall.rs forward to syscall_table::dispatch with one canonical syscall number map.

issues.problem: sys_read() and sys_write() dereference arbitrary user pointers without validating address ranges or mappings.
issues.failure_scenario: A user process can pass an invalid pointer and crash the kernel, or pass kernel memory and read/write privileged data.
issues.fix_instruction: Introduce copy_to_user/copy_from_user helpers that validate user virtual ranges before any slice or pointer write.

issues.problem: sys_open() and sys_close() return success without doing anything.
issues.failure_scenario: User programs believe files opened or closed successfully while no descriptor table state changed.
issues.fix_instruction: Return -ENOSYS until the operations are implemented, or wire them to VFS file descriptor management.
issues.suggested_code:
fn sys_open(_path_ptr: usize, _flags: usize) -> isize { -38 }
fn sys_close(_fd: usize) -> isize { -38 }

issues.problem: sys_exit() spins forever instead of marking the current task exited and scheduling another task.
issues.failure_scenario: A process calling exit consumes CPU forever and never releases resources.
issues.fix_instruction: Mark the current task dead, release owned resources, and invoke the scheduler. If no task remains, halt the CPU.

issues.problem: create() allocates zero bytes for every new regular file. alloc_data(0) returns the same offset repeatedly, so files alias the same backing storage.
issues.failure_scenario: Writing to one newly created tmpfs file overwrites data visible through another file.
issues.fix_instruction: Track per-file capacity and allocate storage on first write or reserve a nonzero extent for each file.
issues.suggested_code:
// Minimal direction: add a capacity field to Inode and allocate on write when
// capacity is insufficient; never call alloc_data(0) as a unique file extent.

issues.problem: remove() marks inodes inactive but never releases their data extents.
issues.failure_scenario: Long-running systems that create and delete temporary files eventually exhaust tmpfs data space.
issues.fix_instruction: Add extent tracking/free-list support or document tmpfs as append-only until reboot.

issues.problem: Global mount and file descriptor tables are mutable statics without synchronization.
issues.failure_scenario: Concurrent syscalls or interrupts can mutate VFS state at the same time and corrupt mount or fd table entries.
issues.fix_instruction: Replace static mut tables with an interrupt-safe lock around VFS state, and avoid returning references that outlive the lock.
issues.suggested_code: static VFS_STATE: spin::Mutex<VfsState> = spin::Mutex::new(VfsState::new());

issues.problem: umount() removes a mount without checking whether file descriptors under that mount are still open.
issues.failure_scenario: Open file descriptors can point to a filesystem that has been unmounted, causing later read/write calls to target invalid state.
issues.fix_instruction: Track mount references/open files and return busy when any fd belongs to the mount being unmounted.

issues.problem: Integration tests use normal #[test] functions against a no_std/no_main kernel crate. cargo test --target x86_64-unknown-none fails because the test crate and panic handler are unavailable.
issues.failure_scenario: CI cannot run kernel tests on the configured bare-metal target.
issues.fix_instruction: Move pure logic into a host-testable library with hardware modules cfg-gated, or implement a custom no_std test harness for QEMU-based tests.
